summary: Intermittent 5xx spike: IPv6 dual-stack routing misroute causing upstream runtime connection resets and crashloops during embedding microbursts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:18 UTC NimbleScribe reported elevated 5xx rates on embedding routes. Impact: Several production customers received 502/504/5xx errors and experienced increased end-to-end latency for embedding upload and streaming embed endpoints. Symptoms: Rapid series of connection resets from the api-gateway to the serving runtime, followed by runtime process restarts (OOM not reported) and an elevated 5xx floor that resolved only after manual route adjustment.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent embedding requests (payloads ~2-8MB) to /v1/embeddings with concurrency > 80 from a single tenant ID; 2) Ensure client uses dual-stack network (IPv4+IPv6); 3) Observe intermittent 5xx responses back from the API gateway and sporadic connection reset logs between apigw and runtime; 4) Reproduce window lasts ~1-6 minutes depending on traffic shape.

[2026-03-12T09:17:56Z] apigw: upstream write failed: connection reset by peer (v6->v4 fallback)

timeline:
2026-03-12 09:16 UTC - NimbleScribe reports first error surge via support form.
2026-03-12 09:17 UTC - Support triage; assigned P1 to SRE (Marcus).
2026-03-12 09:18 UTC - Metrics show 5xx spike from api-gateway to serving-runtime; spike correlates with embedding bulk uploads.
2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Pager: SRE and Network on-call paged.
2026-03-12 09:23 UTC - Hypothesis formed: network path preferred IPv6 for a subset of hosts; subsequent connections falling back and causing half-open sockets.
2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Mitigation: temporarily disabled IPv6 outbound on gateway egress to affected runtime pool; immediate drop in 5xx observed.
2026-03-12 11:05 UTC - Deployed permanent routing fix and small apigw retry tweak (reducing hedged retries).
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Customer confirmed normal behavior; ticket moved to Resolved on 2026-03-13 after post-deploy monitoring.
investigation_notes: Initial metrics: 5xx rate rose from baseline 0.3% to 11% on /v1/embeddings for tenant nimble-123 during the microburst window.
Network capture between apigw and runtime showed TCP RSTs when apigw attempted to reuse IPv6 sockets to a particular runtime subnet; immediate fallback to IPv4 created rapid connection churn.

Runtime process restarts traced to tight socket queue exhaustion and abrupt accept() failures — not to out-of-memory. Logs show accept queue reset followed by graceful shutdown sequence of runtime worker processes.
Reproduced internally with a synthetic client that alternated IPv6/IPv4 flows; observed the same pattern of accept-queue pressure and 502 responses until IPv6 egress was disabled.

Config bug: a recent network policy change (PR #9842) altered the IP preferences in the egress host route table for the apigw pool in us-east, introducing a race where IPv6 routes intermittently became preferred for a subset of requests.

Hedged-retry behavior in apigw amplified the fault by creating parallel connections across v6/v4 which increased in-flight sockets and caused accept queue overruns on runtimes under embedding payload stress.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: disabled IPv6 egress for the affected apigw pool in us-east and reduced hedged retry concurrency for embedding routes. Root cause fix: rolled back the host-route preference change and added a network-policy assertion to prevent preferential IPv6 failovers. Also hardened runtime accept queue handling to drop half-open attempts more quickly. Deployed runtime patch and egress route rollback 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC. Follow-up: create automation to detect v6/v4 fallback rates >0.5% in 1m and trigger an alert; update runbook for embedding microbursts with networking steps. Customer notified and confirmed recovery.
